title: Paddy Power cuts 1,400 jobs and blames betting tax rises
text:
Paddy Power-owner Flutter has announced plans to cut up to 1,400 jobs as its boss claimed the company "cannot fully absorb" tax rises imposed on the gambling industry.
Staff based in Leeds and Dublin, as well as workers for its UK and Ireland business at Flutter's Portugal and Romania sites, will be most affected, but what roles are at risk has not been disclosed.
The government announced taxes rises on online casino and sports betting, with an exemption for horse racing, in the Budget last year.
Flutter boss Kevin Harrington said the tax hikes had "fundamentally changed" the economic model of the UK betting and gaming industry, arguing it had helped "fuel the unlicensed, unregulated market".
"We continue to expect these tax increases to have a very significant impact on the overall market," Flutter Entertainment said on Tuesday.
Flutter, which also owns Sky Bet and Betfair, employs 28,500 people across the world, including 9,000 in the UK and Ireland.
As well as its Leeds and Dublin offices, the BBC understands the cuts could also affect staff based in London and Sunderland, as well as Malta and Gibraltar.
Harrington, who is chief executive of the betting giant's UK and Ireland business, said: "As we warned a year ago, we cannot fully absorb a rise of this magnitude without reducing our fixed cost base and therefore must restructure our business so that we can best position ourselves for the future."
The BBC has contacted the Treasury for comment.
Flutter delisted from the London Stock Exchange in August in a blow to the UK, with its shares now solely traded in New York.
In its most recent results, the company reported a $299m (Â£224m) pre-tax loss for the three months to June for its entire business worldwide, compared to a $205m profit in the same period last year. Sales rose 3% to $4.3bn.
However, revenues in the UK and Ireland rose by 4% over the period, due to strong growth in online gambling games.
Some online gambling tax rises announced in last year's Budget took effect in April. This included remote gaming duty, which is paid on online casino betting, rising from 21% to 40%.
General betting duty, paid on the profits made from various forms of sports betting, was kept at 15% in betting shops, but is set to rise from 15% to 25% online in April next year.
Betting firms had warned that cost increases would lead to job losses and betting shop closures, but MPs dismissed the warnings as "scaremongering".
During the summer, Ladbrokes owner Entain announced job cuts, with news agency Reuters reporting 500 roles were being removed.
Punters' winnings from gambling are not taxed in the UK, nor is VAT charged on bets.
Flutter said its restructuring plan would cost between $80m and $90m.
The company has claimed in previous financial results that the impact of UK tax rises would hit its underlying profit by $320m this year and $540m in 2027, before any savings or restructure to mitigate the impact.

title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office
text:
The Unite union has hit out at a plan by NatWest to reduce the rights of 30,000 of its employees to work from home.
NatWest says it is moving to a hybrid approach where workers will be required to attend the office at least two days a week, from February.
The bank says this is still very competitive with the rest of the finance industry, and exceptions will be made for colleagues who require additional flexibility.
But Unite said NatWest's decision was "out of touch with the realities facing its workforce", with many facing higher travel and childcare costs.
Firms have been gradually drawing people back into the office since working from home became the norm for some office workers during the Covid pandemic.
In January last year, Amazon required staff to return to the office five days a week after they had been working two days at home.
Other firms such as Boots and JP Morgan have brought in policies requiring head office staff to be in every day.
But Barclays faced a backlash from staff last month over plans to require workers to go to the office three days a week. It brought in a longer transition period in response to staff and union complaints.
Unite said NatWest was abolishing its "remote first" employment category, which allows 13,497 workers to attend the office around twice a month, and requiring 17,272 hybrid workers to increase their office attendance.
The union says that many of the affected workers are lower-paid grades, and the new requirements will increase cost-of-living pressures, while disrupting the arrangements of disabled workers and carers.
In a statement, Unite general secretary Sharon Graham called NatWest's move a "kick in the teeth" for its workers.
"Thousands of workers face higher travel and childcare costs and disruption to caring responsibilities," she said
"For NatWest to impose these changes while reneging on existing agreements shows complete contempt for its workforce."
Graham called on NatWest to "ditch these proposals and engage properly with its workers".
A NatWest spokesman said: "Flexible working remains an important part of how we work but we've also learned more about the value that spending time together brings for our colleagues and customers - helping teams collaborate, share ideas, build relationships and learn from one another.
"That's why we're introducing a more consistent approach across the bank, with colleagues expected to spend at least two days a week in the office, depending on the needs of their role and business area.
"We recognise this will be a change for some colleagues and we're giving them time to plan ahead and will support them through the transition."

title: Jobless rate falls but small firms cut back hiring
text:
The UK's unemployment rate has dropped to its lowest for more than year, but job vacancies have continued to fall as smaller businesses cut back on recruitment, official figures indicate.
The jobless rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said, the lowest since July last year.
However, vacancies fell by 21,000 in the three months to September to 691,000, with the ONS saying small firms were citing labour costs as a key factor in scaling back hiring.
The figures are the last official snapshot of the jobs market before the Budget, and  analysts said they indicated the jobs market was showing signs of recovery despite the weakness in hiring.
ONS deputy director of labour market statistics, David Freeman, said the labour market remained "broadly flat", with the latest data showing the employment rate edging up and "a small drop in unemployment".
"The number of workers on payroll remains slightly down over the same period, though data for the most recent month suggests that might be starting to level off," he said.
"The number of vacancies has seen its largest fall since the start of the year, concentrated mainly within smaller businesses, which cite increased labour costs as a key factor."
Energy costs have risen since the Iran war began, and companies have also said that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made it more expensive to employ staff.
The number of job vacancies fell to its lowest level in more than five years, the figures indicated, with the largest decrease in construction jobs.
Average earnings excluding bonuses rose 3.7% in the three months to August, up from 3.5% last month. Taking inflation into account, wages grew 0.8% in real terms.
Pat McFadden, the Secretary of State for Work and Pensions, said the figures "show the resilience of our labour market" with the UK's employment rate "now the third highest in the G7, despite a backdrop of global uncertainty".
However, he said that "too many young people still find themselves locked out of employment".
The government is working with industry "to bring young people back into the labour market and prevent them from drifting into the welfare system", he added.
But Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said on X , external that "businesses can't afford to hire".
"This is what happens when you attack employers, tax jobs, and put up red tape," he said.
The latest ONS figures showed the unemployment rate for those aged 16 to 24 was 15.6% in the June to August quarter. While that was down from 16.4% in the  March to May period, it was still higher than the rate of 14.6% seen in the June-to-August period last year.
Separate ONS figures have indicated that nearly one million young people in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet"
On Monday, Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned the UK faces an "economic catastrophe and moral failure" due to high levels of youth unemployment.
Ashley Webb, senior UK economist for Capital Economics, said the fall in the unemployment rate was "unexpected", and that it suggests the labour market "continues to recover".
But "with businesses' energy costs likely to fall only slowly, we still think hiring will stay subdued," he said.
Louise Murphy, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said the labour market "has performed poorly in recent years as the number of jobs has fallen and pay growth weakened".
But she added that the UK's "recent bout of economic resilience may finally be creating some green shoots", pointing to "rising employment levels and private sector wage growth stabilising".
The quality of ONS statistics has been criticised in recent years, with a review last year finding "deep seated" issues with the body .
The Labour Force Survey, which it uses to report payroll and employment figures, has suffered from low response rates.
In an update on Tuesday, the ONS said that response levels had improved, but that "some volatility" remained in the statistics.

title: Chancellor rejects calls to raise Capital Gains Tax in Budget
text:
Chancellor John Healey says he wants to avoid an investor exodus from the UK
Chancellor John Healey has dismissed calls from some Labour MPs to increase Capital Gains Tax (CGT).
Cabinet ministers Wes Streeting and Louise Haigh both previously voiced support for raising CGT before Andy Burnham became prime minister in July.
Ahead of next week's Budget, as first reported by the Times , external , Healey is minded not to increase CGT - which is imposed on the profit people make when they sell an asset that has increased in value, such as shares in a company or properties which are not primary residences.
The move followed warnings that it could end up costing the government money if wealthy people leave the country or defer selling off assets.
If you pay income tax at the basic rate then CGT is charged at 18%. For higher and additional rate income tax payers, the CGT rate is 24%.
Last year, HMRC estimated , external that lifting the lower rate of CGT by 1% could raise Â£5m by 2028-9 but increasing the higher rate of CGT by 10% would reduce the Treasury's receipts by Â£3.6bn in 2028-9.
The amount raised could be reduced if people adapt their behaviour to the tax rise, for example by moving abroad or deciding not to sell a property.
The chancellor gave an indication of his approach last month in a speech when he spoke about the importance of businesses and self-employed people making profits.
"I want to see this country as a country of wealth creation. I want our government decisions and policies to raise the levels of confidence, and investment, and profit in British business," Healey said.
Burnham has faced warnings against lifting CGT. His former adviser and Goldman Sachs Chief Economist Lord Jim O'Neill suggested it would send "the wrong message to business".
But influential Labour figures had pushed for equalising CGT and income tax, with the former generally attracting a lower tax rate.
Louise Haigh, a key ally of the prime minister, had suggested capital gains should go up to be closer to income tax, before she became Burnham's first secretary of state.
In an article for the Renewal journal, , external Haigh argued that raising CGT would "shift the taxation burden away from punishing work, and towards unproductive capital accumulation which does little to grow the everyday economy".
She said this could be accompanied by measures to ensure that "genuine investment returns are not penalised".
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called for a "wealth tax that works" in May, shortly after resigning as a minister in former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer's government.
He had argued that equalising CGT with income tax would address an unfair system that was "penalising work".
Healey had already ruled out levelling the two tax rates, according to a report in the Financial Times last week , external .
Asked about the government's plans for CGT on BBC Breakfast, Communities Secretary Angela Rayner would not speculate on the Budget.
Pressed over whether rejecting calls to increase the tax was a win for the rich, she said the government had already taken steps to give people "breathing space" and help with the cost of living.
It comes after senior banking executives told the BBC they expect Healey to raise taxes on the sector. UK banks have been reporting bumper profits, leading to calls from unions for higher taxes.
Healey is due to set out his tax and spending plans at his first Budget on 28 October, against the backdrop of the US-Iran war which has led to rising prices.
The chancellor is under pressure to find measures to ease the cost of living and fund an increase for defence at his spending review next year.
The chancellor's options for raising money are limited as Labour's 2024 manifesto pledged not to increase income tax, National Insurance and VAT, the three big revenue raisers.
The government is also restricted in how much it can borrow due to its self-imposed rules on debt.
In a pre-Budget speech on Tuesday, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch urged the government to cut spending and reduce its borrowing.
She said the prime minister and the chancellor should "live within our means" and pointed to her party's plan to save Â£70bn in cuts, including to welfare and overseas development aid.
Badenoch told an audience in central London that Labour would not "find the courage" to cut spending.
She said the chancellor wanted to deliver a "nothing to see here Budget" but added: "Britain cannot afford to do as little as possible."
The Liberal Democrats have said the government could raise Â£14bn partly by introducing a windfall tax on the profits of banks.
The party's deputy leader Daisy Cooper said the money could go towards cutting fuel duty, rail and bus fares and VAT for hospitality businesses.

title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules
text:
Drivers will be given the right to challenge "rip-off" private parking charges and more grace when using private providers under new rules set out by Andy Burnham.
The prime minister announced the changes after concerns were raised that penalties issued by private providers were too harsh and left motorists unfairly punished.
The new rules include a cancellation of charges for honest mistakes such as stopping to check directions and for non-payment due to broken ticket machines. Drivers will also get a 10-minute window to leave a car park without facing a penalty.
Motoring groups welcomed the changes, but said more needed to be done to stop charges when the driver had done nothing wrong.
Private car parks are different to council-owned car parks and streets, but more tickets at private sites are now being issued than ever recorded.
According to RAC analysis of government data, some 17 million private parking tickets were issued in 2025-26, a 17% increase from a year earlier.
With each charge worth up to Â£100, the data suggests drivers could collectively face private parking charges worth more than Â£4.6m each day.
In one case, a woman was taken to court in a Â£1,906 claim after taking longer than five minutes to pay at a car park in Derby . The charge was eventually dropped .
"Being a few minutes late back to your car or typing one digit of your number plate wrong shouldn't end with a hefty fine landing on your doormat," said Burnham.
He added that such charges left "people feeling ripped off and out of pocket".
A guaranteed five-minute period to decide whether to park
A 10-minute window to leave without facing a penalty
Cancellation of charges for issues drivers can't control, such as vehicle breakdowns in car parks
Cancellation of charges for honest mistakes such as stopping to check directions, as well as for medical emergencies or broken ticket machines
Maximum charges of Â£20 on appeal for slip-ups such as forgetting a parking permit, entering the wrong vehicle registration, or forgetting to confirm the registration in the machine when parking
A freeze on the maximum parking charge at Â£100, which is the same limit as the current private parking Code of Practice
The new code will apply in England, Scotland and Wales.
Operators who do not comply risk losing access to DVLA data, making it more difficult to pursue the car's owner even if they do issue a charge.
'I got fined Â£11k over a five-minute parking rule'
Firm told to pay Â£10,240 in five-minute parking row
The government's Private Parking Code of Practice has been seven years in the making.
In 2019, an act of Parliament was passed to create a code but the code was withdrawn in 2022, due to "resistance from the private parking industry", according to the RAC.
The current industry Code of Practice, created by the British Parking Association and the International Parking Community, was introduced in 2024 and updated last year after a review .
Angela Rayner, the Communities and Housing Secretary, told BBC Breakfast that parking "shouldn't be a way of making money".
Asked if the changes were an admission that motorists have been "ripped off" by parking companies for years, she said: "We're calling time on it. They have regulated themselves and they have their appeals process but we're giving it more meat now."
She said the current level of fine was a "proportionate response to when people don't follow the rules".
Derek Millard-Smith from the British Parking Association said the group welcomed the changes as it would "increase trust" and said "detterents work" when it came to questions over the cost of fines.
"We know dog fouling, rail fare dodging, littering - all those levels are around Â£100 or more because that is a level that is deemed sufficient to change behaviours."
Both the AA and the RAC said the new code was a good first step but did not go far enough.
The AA said some drivers pay up even if they have done nothing wrong, just to avoid the hassle and over fears of legal action being taken against them.
"There is still a huge amount of work to do, such as tackling the scourge of debt recovery fees," added Jack Cousens, head of roads policy at the AA.
"Ultimately, we need to stop charges being issued in the first place, especially where the driver has done nothing wrong."
The RAC's head of policy, Simon Williams, called for the banning of debt recovery fees and said the current industry-run appeals bodies should be replaced by a single independent one.
The government said it would be consulting on the issue of debt recovery fees, as well as other recommendations from the Competition and Markets Authority.

title: ICICI Prudential Life Insurance to focus on growing absolute VNB amid slump in FY24
text:
ICICI Prudential Life Insurance said it will focus on growing its absolute Value of New Business (VNB) moving forward. In the Q4FY24 results announced on April 23, the company said VNB, which is the expected profitability from new policies sold, fell 19.45 percent to Rs 2,227 crore for FY24 from Rs 2,765 crore in FY23. VNB margin also fell to 24.6 percent in FY24 from 32 percent in the previous year.
Dhiren Salian, Chief Financial Officer of the company, said in the post-earnings conference call that the decline in VNB is due to shift in “product mix, competitive pricing pressures and increases in expenses”.
An increase in stock market buoyancy has led to investors choosing unit- linked portfolios, which is a low-margin product. Salian also said the change in taxation of more than Rs 5 lakh non-linked policies impacted the insurance industries.
Costs have also increased for ICICI Prudential Life Insurance as a redesign in the commission structure has led to higher commission expenses, further weighing down on margin.
Sailan said the impact of the revised commission has been factored in the year and unit cost will not to be impacted much going forward.
The insurer’s Annual Premium Equivalent (APE), which is a measure of sales for insurance companies, increased 4.69 percent to Rs 9046 crore in FY2024.
In the Q4 results of the company that announced after market hours, the company’s net profit fell 26 percent YoY to Rs 174 crore in the quarter that ended in March 2024.
The board also declared a final dividend of Rs 0.6 per equity share of face value of Rs 10 each, to the shareholders.

title: Tata Elxsi Q4 net profit, revenue decline QoQ; firm declares dividend of Rs 70 per share
text:
Design and technology services company Tata Elxsi on April 23 reported a net profit of Rs 196.93 crore for the quarter ended March 31, declining both sequentially and annually, according to an exchange filing.
The company also announced a dividend of Rs 70 per share for the financial year 2023-24, it said.
“Further, we are pleased to inform you that the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of 700% at Rs 70 per equity share of Rs 10 each, for the financial year 2023-24, subject to tax, which shall be paid/dispatched on or after the seventh day from the conclusion of the 35th Annual General Meeting, subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company,” the firm announced.
The net profit was down 4.6 percent quarter-on-quarter compared to Rs 206.4 crore reported in the October to December period of FY24 and lower by 2.32 percent against Rs 201.5 crore in the March quarter of FY23, the filing showed.
The company’s total revenue from operations stood at Rs 905.9 crore in the March quarter, which was lower compared to Rs 914.23 crore in Q3FY24, but higher than Rs 837.91 crore recorded in Q4FY23.
For the full year, the company reported a profit after tax of Rs 792.2 crore in FY24, jumping 4.9 percent YoY and a revenue of Rs 3,552.1 crore, gaining 13 percent YoY.
"I am pleased with our overall performance and resilience in revenues, margins, and customer additions through the year in a volatile macroeconomic environment. We are entering the new financial year with a
strong commitment for growth, and continued confidence in our differentiated design-led engineering capabilities. This is backed by strong customer relationships, addition of marquee logos, large deal wins,
especially in SDV, investments in AI and GenAI, and a strong deal pipeline for the year ahead,” said company's CEO and MD Manoj Raghavan.
In terms of sectors, the company's transportation segment recorded a growth of 20.4 percent YoY in CC terms, It was supported by large deals and
sustained traction in software defined vehicles, the company said.
Healthcare and media & communications segments also posted growths of 7.6 percent and 2.6 percent YoY respectively.
The company also added 178 employees compared to the previous quarter, taking the total headcount to 13,399 at the end of the March quarter. The attrition rate for the said quarter was at 12.4 percent, down from 12.9 percent in the December quarter, the company said.
The Bengaluru-based company’s stock price ended marginally lower by 0.57 percent at Rs 7,393.85 on BSE on April 23.

title: ICICI Pru Life Q4 net profit falls 26% to Rs 174 cr, insurer announces dividend
text:
ICICI Prudential Life Insurance on April 23 reported 26% drop in net profit at Rs 174 crore for the quarter ended March 31, 2024. It reported net profit of Rs 235 crore in the year-ago period.
The insurer's net premium income rose 17% to Rs 14,788 crore in Q4FY24 as against Rs 12,629 crore in Q4FY23.
The insurer said its Board approved final dividend of 60 paise per equity share of face value of Rs 10 each to its shareholders.
The insurer's solvency ratio was at 191.8% in Q4FY24 as compared to 208.9% in the year-ago period.
On April 23, ICICI Prudential's shares on BSE closed trading 3% higher at Rs 597.85 apiece.
The annual premium equivalent (APE) of the insurer was up 9.5 percent on a year-on-year (YoY) basis at Rs 3,615 crore vs Rs 3,300 crore. APE is a metric used to measure new business sales growth.
Value of new business (VNB) was down 26.5 percent at Rs 776 crore vs Rs 1,055 crore and VNB margin stood at 21.5 percent vs 32 percent. VNB is a measure of the profit margin of new business written by a life insurance company.
At the end of financial year 2023-24, the total assets under management of the insurer were at Rs 2.94 lakh crore versus Rs 2.51 lakh crore.

title: Cyient DLM#39;s profit after tax in FY24 surges 93%
text:
Cyient DLM reported a strong 92.9 percent surge in profit after tax to Rs 61.2 crore for the financial year 2023-24, according to an exchange filing issued on April 23.
The company posted a revenue of Rs 362 crore for the quarter ended March 31, 2024, recording a growth of 12.7 percent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and 30.5 percent year-on-year (YoY), the filing showed. For the full year, revenue stood at Rs 1,192 crore, which was 43.2 percent higher compared to the same period of the past financial year.
The firm’s EBITDA for FY24 was at Rs 111 crore, with a margin of 9.3 percent and YoY growth of 26.5 percent, the company statement said.
Anthony Montalbano, chief executive officer, Cyient DLM, said, “Cyient DLM business focus remains on strengthening our capabilities and expanding our customer base. The robust growth for this year was led by aerospace and defence (A&D) segments. Large deals in A&D constitute major portion of Order Book and pipeline and are expected to contribute towards FY25 & FY26 growth."
The company further said that the outlook for FY25 “continues to remain strong and it expects strong growth backed by order book and strong relationships with key clients”. It also said that it will look for expanding its geographical footprint through inorganic expansions.
Cyient DLM is a subsidiary of software service company Cyient. It’s stock price closed on April 23 at Rs 687.35 on the BSE, recording a gain of 2.79 percent.
In FY24, the company added two new logos in A&D and bagged key large deals during the year. It also said that the company has a strong pipeline of projects for the years ahead. The company also added two new facilities in Bengaluru and Mysuru, the filing said.

title: Who is Harish Bhat? Why the Tata veteran resigned from Trent's board and what he told Noel Tata
text:
Harish Bhat , the non-executive and non-independent director at Trent , has resigned from his position, as per a stock exchange filing dated October 18. Bhat's resignation took effect on 17 October. In his resignation letter to Chairman Noel Tata , Harish Bhat revealed the reason behind his decision. He cited growing personal and professional commitments as the reason behind his decision. Bhat wrote in the letter, as per Business Standard, “I am writing this letter to communicate my decision to resign from the Board of Directors of Trent Ltd., due to my existing and growing professional and personal commitments.” In the same letter, Harish Bhatt also talked about Chairman Noel Tata. He expressed his pleasure in serving on the board of Trent Ltd over the years. He praised Noel Tata for his leadership as well. “I have greatly admired your leadership, which has been instrumental in the rapid growth and transformation of the company,” Bhat added. Furthermore, Bhat thanked the board for the opportunity to serve Trent. Harish Bhat serves as the Brand Custodian at Tata Sons, bringing over 35 years of leadership to the group since his joining as a Tata Administrative Service (TAS) officer in 1987. He was the Chairman of Tata Coffee Limited and was a part of the boards of several major group companies, including Trent Ltd, Tata Starbucks Pvt Ltd, Infiniti Retail Ltd, and Tata AIA Life Insurance Company Limited. Throughout his extensive career as the company executive, Bhat has held several executive positions such as Managing Director of Tata Global Beverages Ltd and Chief Operating Officer for both the telecom business and the Watches and Jewellery divisions of Titan Company Ltd. In the last two decades, he played a key role in major corporate strategies, including the group's jewellery business, playing a central role in the acquisition of Tetley, and the launch and growth of numerous Tata brands. Mr Bhat graduated from both BITS Pilani and IIM Ahmedabad, where he bagged the prestigious IIM Ahmedabad Gold Medal in 1987. He also earned the British Government's Chevening Scholarship for young managers a decade later, followed by the BITS Pilani Distinguished Alumnus Award in 2017. Apart from his corporate duties, Bhat previously served as a member of the Consumer Insights Panel for the Government of Singapore’s Economic Development Board. Mr Bhat is also an avid reader and a writer who regularly contributes articles to top national publications. He is the author of four published books, including his recent national bestseller, "#Tata Stories", which focused on 40 inspiring tales from the history of the Tata Group, as per the official website of the company. Sneha Biswas specialises in covering entertainment and pop culture, with a specialisation on Bollywood, Hollywood, OTT platforms, K-pop, K-dramas, and major developments in the US entertainment industry. She believes in telling stories that balance speed with substance, and in making entertainment journalism contextual, culturally aware, and reader-first rather than purely reactive.

With over six years of experience in digital media, Sneha currently serves as a Deputy Chief Content Producer at Live Mint. She has spent more than three and a half years with the HT Group and returned to the organisation in February 2025, joining Live Mint to uplift the entertainment section. Over the past year, she has been closely involved in entertainment coverage including breaking news, explainers, trend reporting, box office reports and analysis for the audience.

Sneha is Google News certified, having completed training focused on newsroom best practices, digital reporting, and SEO-driven content strategies. Her work reflects a strong understanding of audience behaviour, search trends, and the evolving consumption patterns of entertainment news across formats.

Prior to her current role, Sneha has worked across multiple content and editorial functions within digital newsrooms, building expertise in content planning, editing, and real-time coverage. Her professional interests lie at the intersection of entertainment, internet culture, and global pop trends.

Working for the National city team, Biswas closely follows global entertainment movements while maintaining a strong pulse on what is happening in India. title: Akash Ambani: from building Jio to selling its story
text:
Akash Ambani would rather talk technology than himself. In an email interview ahead of the company's initial public offering opening on Wednesday, the managing director of Jio Platforms focuses on scale, technology and the promise of long-term value, drawing heavily on the Jio story his father Mukesh Ambani built.
Akash comes across as a technology enthusiast who spent the past decade in the trenches, helping build Jio from its 2016 launch into one of India’s most consequential digital businesses. This quiet confidence comes from being part of the grind, where ambition was matched by execution at extraordinary scale. For Akash, Jio is not just a telecom giant; it is a technology company built on an indigenous stack, with connectivity as its foundation.
As Jio prepares for what could be India’s biggest IPO , he is stepping into a new role: telling its story to public-market investors alongside his sister, Isha. The stakes are real: Akash must now convince investors he can do more than carry forward his father’s legacy—that he can turn Jio’s extraordinary scale into enduring value for millions of shareholders.
As Jio Platforms’ managing director, Akash Ambani is helping present the company’s story to public-market investors alongside his sister, Isha. He has emphasized Jio’s technology capabilities, scale and long-term value.
Jio identifies home broadband, fixed wireless access, enterprise services, cloud and other digital offerings as growth opportunities. Its connectivity business remains the financial backbone, while the company says it will report progress on value-added services and overseas managed services after listing.
The IPO is a fresh issue, with proceeds primarily intended to repay or prepay borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm. The main article says the listing is expected to leave Jio Platforms with a net-debt-free balance sheet.
Akash says Jio aims to raise value per customer through services that combine connectivity with digital applications, rather than relying only on higher charges per gigabyte. He said the company has no five-year ARPU target and will assess offerings against customer needs, usage and service quality.
The articles identify ARPU growth, monetization of digital services and returns on capital as important measures. Investors can also track whether Jio’s growth in broadband, enterprise and other services translates into stronger returns.
Our message to retail investors is to understand Jio Platforms as a long-term technology and digital services business, which has multiple growth engines. With India’s rapid digitalization and mass adoption of next-gen digital technologies, Jio has a very large and expanding target addressable market in the form of growing mobile data usage, migrating customers to higher-quality digital experiences, expanding home broadband and fixed wireless access, deepening enterprise relationships.
We will be happy to report our progress with the value-added services, and overseas managed services from time-to-time post-listing.
Capital discipline is part of how we build. The net-debt-free balance sheet post-IPO will be a great strength for Jio Platforms, with operations generating increasingly higher amounts of free cash flows. Our current and growing free cash flows have already been deleveraging: our net debt to Ebitda came down from 0.88x in FY24 to 0.36x in FY26. Ultimately, the FCF will chase growth and create great value for the new investors joining the Jio family. With strong internal cash flows significantly greater than the investment requirements, we don’t foresee a need to approach equity markets in the near or mid-term.
We grow value per customer by giving people more to do on our network, not only by charging more per gigabyte. At Jio, our objective is to create greater value from our network capabilities for both customers and shareholders. We do not see network monetization as being limited to charging more for every gigabyte of data. Instead, our focus is on offering value-added services that combine connectivity with digital applications and other capabilities. Our customers already use 43.7 GB of data a month on average, and are consuming 333 million digital services subscriptions.
I’d rather not compare us with other operators, as the definition of Arpu and business model varies across operators.
We do not have any five-year Arpu target. We believe that revenue growth must be supported by sustainable customer value, not viewed in isolation. Hence, our future offerings will be assessed in the context of customer needs, usage patterns, service quality, and the evolving market.
The IPO represents an important milestone in Reliance Group’s journey. It brings Jio Platforms into the public markets and gives public-market investors an opportunity to evaluate and participate in the company’s future. We hope the listing will reinforce confidence in India’s technology capabilities and in the opportunities created by the country’s digital transformation.
As regards the IPO process, my father Mr Mukesh Ambani, as well as all the directors on RIL’s board, gave a lot of insights as well as valuable advice. We also have an experienced and capable team of leaders, as well as professional advisors and lead managers, who managed the IPO process extremely well.
Technology is my passion, and hence, I could relate with telecom and technology businesses pretty well. However, we must note that all three of us are involved in each business together, and always count on each other to back up when needed.
Jio’s story was already very well-known across the world, and there has long been a high level of interest about Jio’s journey; so, our presentations were extremely well-received. What I take from my grandfather, Dhirubhai Ambani, is respect for every shareholder and generating returns for them.
Through the roadshows, we have had the opportunity to explain Jio Platforms’ business, technology capabilities, financial performance and long-term opportunities to investors from all over the world. Their response has been overwhelmingly positive.
Looking at the institutional interest in the IPO and the record subscription to the anchor book, I’d like to believe that we were able to convey Jio’s story well.
Reliance has a remarkable history of creating opportunities for ordinary Indians to participate in its growth. That relationship is built on trust, long-term thinking and the belief that the benefits of enterprise should extend beyond the company itself.
We are entering the public markets with a responsibility to build a strong, sustainable business and create immense value over time. We are committed to innovation, execution, financial discipline and the transparency expected of a listed company.
For the next generation of Indian builders, I hope it shows that deep technology can be built in India, by Indians, at scale.
At its core, Jio is a digital services company built on the foundation of connectivity. We have built capabilities across 5G and home broadband, cloud, devices, software, entertainment, and enterprise services. These are supported by a proprietary technology stack that Jio has designed, developed, and deployed in-house. This gives us greater control over our services and operations and enables us to offer our customers a value proposition with no parallel in India.
And that is how we built Jio: as a technology company that uses connectivity as its foundation. On it, we have added connectivity, digital services, all on a stack we designed and deployed in-house, with more than 12,000 people in our digital products and technology teams.
Reliance was built to create world-class companies from India. We have done that across all our businesses by delivering unbeatable customer value and operating at world-class efficiency. That is exactly why we welcome competition. It brings out the best in us, and the real winners are India’s consumers.
I would look at this constructively. Once the facts were on the table, there was very little left to disagree about. The government applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign, and Jio’s own satellite services are awaiting clearances too, which was clear and acknowledged.
We have always believed in working with partners across the global technology ecosystem, while staying firmly committed to India’s laws, its regulatory framework and its consumers.

title: Schaeffler India CEO Harsha Gopal Kadam taken into custody over factory accident that killed 2 workers
text:
Schaeffler India CEO and Managing Director Harsha Gopal Kadam was taken into custody on October 19 as part of a probe into a fatal accident at the company's Talegaon facility in Pune in June, the company disclosed in an exchange filing on Tuesday.
The incident took place on June 9, 2026, when a sudden release of carbon dioxide gas during a scheduled cylinder replacement killed two workers employed by a service provider to the company. Kadam was taken into custody by the Talegaon MIDC Police Station late Monday for investigation into the case.
In its exchange filing, Schaeffler India said Kadam had been taken into custody for investigation by the Talegaon MIDC Police Station, under the Pimpri Chinchwad Police Commissionerate, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita , 2023.
The company said it and its officers had cooperated with the investigation and would continue to do so.
"The Company is evaluating the developments in consultation with its legal advisors, has complied and continues to comply with all laws applicable to it and will take all steps necessary in accordance with applicable law to resolve the situation," it said.
Despite the development, Schaeffler India said its business operations continued in the ordinary course.
In its regulatory filing, the company further said that the scope of the investigation had been expanded to include Kadam on the basis that he is considered the "occupier" of the factory premises under applicable law. The company said it, its employees and officers, along with the managing director, had been cooperating with the authorities. Kadam was taken into custody at around 6.40 pm on October 19, according to the filing.
The company added that its senior management continues to oversee day-to-day operations and that business activities remain unaffected. It is evaluating the developments in consultation with its legal advisers.

title: Who is Eric Schmidt? Meet ex-Google CEO whose 1% Anthropic stake could push his fortune close to $80 billion
text:
Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt is among the early investors in artificial intelligence startup Anthropic, holding an approximately 1% stake in the company, according to a Bloomberg report. His investment, made when the company was valued at just $461 million in 2021, could translate into one of the biggest individual fortunes from Anthropic's anticipated initial public offering (IPO). Schmidt invested tens of millions of dollars in Anthropic's Series A funding round, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter who requested anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss private information. It remains unclear whether he has sold any portion of his original holding. Schmidt and Anthropic declined to comment, the report noted. The potential gains could significantly increase the 71-year-old technology investor's wealth. Based on a possible Anthropic valuation of $2 trillion, his stake could add roughly one-third to his net worth, taking it close to $80 billion, according to Bloomberg's wealth index. Even at Anthropic's more recent valuation of $965 billion, Schmidt's holding could be worth nearly $10 billion, adding substantially to his existing fortune of $57.5 billion. Eric Emerson Schmidt is an American businessman, technology investor and former computer engineer best known for leading Google during a significant period of its expansion. He served as the company's chief executive officer from 2001 to 2011 before becoming its executive chairman, a position he held until 2015. He subsequently served as executive chairman of Google's parent company Alphabet from 2015 to 2017 and remained a technical adviser to the company until 2020. Born on April 27, 1955, in Falls Church, Virginia, Schmidt studied electrical engineering at Princeton University, where he earned a Bachelor of Science in Engineering degree in 1976. He later completed a master's degree in electrical engineering and computer science in 1979 and a PhD in the same field at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1982. Beyond his corporate leadership roles, Schmidt has established himself as a prominent technology investor. His investments have been made through several platforms, including TomorrowVentures, Innovation Endeavors and his family office, Hillspire. His earlier investment portfolio included consumer internet businesses, software companies and financial technology ventures. In recent years, artificial intelligence has become a central focus, with investments in companies such as Mistral AI, Reflection AI, World Labs and Anthropic. Schmidt's early investment could prove particularly lucrative as Anthropic prepares for a potential stock market debut. When he invested in the startup in 2021, Anthropic was valued at approximately $461 million, according to PitchBook data cited by Bloomberg. Investors have since indicated that a valuation between $1.8 trillion and $2 trillion could be possible for the company. At the higher valuation, Anthropic would be worth more than 4,300 times its Series A valuation. The potential returns could also surpass some of Schmidt's earlier successful investments. If Anthropic reaches a $2 trillion valuation, the gains from his stake would exceed the returns from Innovation Endeavors' early investment in Uber Technologies in 2011. Uber's valuation had increased approximately 1,400 times by the time it went public in 2019, reaching $82 billion. Anthropic's anticipated IPO is expected to create substantial wealth for its founders, employees and early investors. The startup's seven co-founders were already worth approximately $8 billion each following its last funding round, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. The company is also backed by major technology players, including Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia and Microsoft, alongside venture capital firms such as Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital. Garvit Bhirani is a journalist based in Gurugram. He is a Deputy Chief Content Producer at LiveMint, where he covers national and international news stories, focusing on accuracy and compelling storytelling for readers.

With a total of six years of experience in journalism, he has previously worked with Vaco Binary Semantics for Google, taking on the role of news curation lead, and reported from the field on health, education, and agriculture stories for 101reporters and News9. He has also served as a content editor for entertainment and news media organisations.

Garvit holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in journalism and mass communication from Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University and Gurugram University, respectively. During college days, he joined India’s only non-profit student journalism network, where he anchored daily news updates and produced his own weekly show called ‘Data Fix’.

He was selected for the YES Foundation Media for Social Change Fellowship in Delhi, the Talking Data to the Fourth Pillar residential workshop, and the VOICE Fellowship in Pune.

He holds certificates in COVID-19-verification reporting, data journalism, food & agriculture, tech policy, media literacy and countering misinformation, and tackling election disinformation courses from Thomson Foundation, IndiaSpend, The Dialogue, US Mission in India, and AFP.

title: Qualcomm layoffs: Chipmaker to cut jobs globally from November after performance reviews
text:
Qualcomm will cut jobs across its global workforce as part of a performance-focused restructuring following its annual employee reviews, with notifications expected to begin in November, Reuters reported on Tuesday.
The report cited a memo from chief executive Cristiano Amon to employees. It did not specify the number of positions that would be eliminated.
Amon said the proposed move was aimed at building a stronger performance culture and addressing cases where employees had consistently fallen short of expectations. The company will consider business priorities, organisational requirements, and the skills and expertise needed for its operations while deciding on the reductions, the memo read.
"As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require," Amon wrote, according to Reuters . "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed," he added.
Qualcomm had approximately 52,000 employees globally as of September 2025, most of them full-time, the Reuters report mentioned further.
The development comes as Qualcomm is navigating weakness in consumer electronics demand, amid rising memory prices. The company is one of the world's largest suppliers of chips for smartphones.
Qualcomm's shares have gained just 1.5% in 2026, compared with a rise of more than 12% in the benchmark S&P 500 and an increase of nearly 60% in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.
In its July earnings report, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below market estimates and said revenue from Apple-related products would decline faster than previously expected.
The company, however, expects growth in data centres and other businesses beyond smartphones to more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. It has been expanding into the artificial intelligence data-centre market as it seeks to diversify beyond its traditional handset business.
Qualcomm expects non-smartphone businesses to account for the majority of its chip sales in fiscal 2027, according to Reuters .
